beats.narration_en: Same car, same wall. One at thirty miles an hour, one at forty.
Only ten faster, but look how much deeper the front crushes.
Crash energy grows with the square of your speed.
So ten more miles an hour means seventy-eight percent more energy.
And every bit of it has to go somewhere.
These steel rails fold like an accordion and turn it into bent metal and heat.
At thirty, they crush about twenty inches.
At forty, nearly twenty-eight. Almost all the way to the cabin.
Hitting a wall at thirty is like falling off a three-story building.
At forty, it's a five-story fall.
Even with braking: where the slower car stops, the faster one is still doing thirty-five.
Same driver, same brakes. Ten miles an hour is the whole difference.
So in town, those ten aren't a little faster. They're almost twice the crash.
